answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to anchor its reputation at a single verified vertex in a trust graph, earned only through costly, observable work. A newcomer must cross a bridge of peer attestations: existing members stake small deposits vouching for it, and if it misbehaves, the vouching stake is slashed. The graph also applies umber-toned decay, so reputation fades unless the agent keeps doing useful verified tasks, and a swarm of idle clones cannot accumulate influence without sustained real contribution.
